Started playing just to see what the game was about.
A few hours later I’m collecting rocks, mining everything in sight and somehow still telling myself “I’ll stop after this one upgrade.”
Really simple but ridiculously addictive. There’s always something to unlock or upgrade, so it’s very easy to lose track of time.
Would recommend if you like games where you can turn your brain off and just grind.

I remember playing this game when I was a kid, and the idea of being able to create so much from so little inspired me in a way. This game is fairly simplistic when starting it, mine, craft, mine more, and so on. However once you begin to explore more of the world, you realize that many solutions often require out-of-the-box thinking, such as the Galaxy puzzles, as well as figuring out optimal setups for resource farming. Although the endgame can be quite lengthy, and 100%'ing takes a good amount of effort, in the end, it's an accomplishment that you will be proud of. I'm so glad I discovered this gem of a game.
It's an extremely addicting game which always has you thinking of new ways to approach the world around you, and that's what I love so much about Forager, and I'm proud to say that after all these years, I've finally reached 100% feat completion. <3

TLDR:
Would I recommend this game? 
Yes, I recommend Forager... Just be aware of the developer situation, leading to an abandoned game before buying.

Forager is a fun and addictive "collect everything" style game with a satisfying gameplay loop. You start with almost nothing and slowly build up your resources, unlock new areas, craft upgrades, and expand your world. The progression feels rewarding, and even after only 2 hours of playtime at the time of writing this review, I can already see why people enjoy it.

That said, potential buyers should be aware of the situation surrounding the game's development. While I personally recommend the game based on the experience I’ve had, the developer behind Forager has a controversial history, including accusations of blaming team members for development issues and poor communication. This is my fourth time in seven years trying to enjoy or at least beat Forager and frankly, it is still a miserable time. Almost completely charmless in its presentation, with terribly designed progression and proc gen that only gets in the way of it being a good time. Forager's main (read "only") strategy to engage the player is what I can only describe as "weaponised overstimulation". You're never given enough time to question what you're doing, why you're doing it or if you're having any fun, because there's always more resources to endlessly mine appearing around you. Exploration is basically non-existant, and there's no way to plan ahead or use any amount of strategy because future skills are only revealed to you immediately before you can choose them. Forager is an adorable casual game but it doesn't stick the landing in a couple of ways that ruined it for me. I first bought this game for Nintendo Switch, and the port was a fail. Once I started buying more land, the frame rate dropped so much it became unplayable and I had to abandon it. (This is the same Switch that can somehow run No Man's Sky, so... c'mon.)

Fast forward to a couple years later, and I was excited to re-purchase Forager for PC when it went on sale--a chance to finally see the end game! Or so I thought. But Forager's pacing falls apart so spectacularly in late game that it left me wondering "Uh, did I beat the game? What else is there to do?" And the answer was that apparently you're supposed to just keep upgrading buildings to use nuclear power and accruing endless gold that you don't even need, all for a few needlessly grindy Feats.
